title: Kaju Katli, Diet Coke and Gold Coins: What India Ordered on Quick Commerce This Diwali
excerpt: Swiggy Instamart's most-ordered mithai was kaju katli, its top non-grocery item on Diwali eve was Diet Coke, and gold coin orders rose 23 times in the week to Dhanteras. Zepto's festive hamper orders tripled, and it delivered 4.68 lakh diyas.
body:
• Kaju katli was Swiggy Instamart's most popular mithai this Diwali, followed by motichoor laddoo and besan laddoo; on Zepto, laddoo was the most frequently ordered sweet and soan papdi led by total quantity.
  • Diet Coke was Instamart's most popular non-grocery item on Diwali eve; its party-planning orders rose 162 percent year on year and snack orders 42 percent.
  • Gold coin orders on Instamart rose 23 times in the week leading up to Dhanteras and silver coin orders seven times; Mumbai recorded the biggest reported festive basket, at Rs 1.11 lakh of gold coins.
  • Zepto's festive hamper orders tripled versus last Diwali, and it recorded 4.68 lakh diya orders during the festive period.

India's Diwali shopping basket moved further onto quick-commerce apps this year, with shoppers ordering everything from mithai and diyas to gold coins on platforms built for ten-minute grocery runs. Data shared by Swiggy Instamart and Zepto, reported by Channel IAM and The Hindu BusinessLine, shows the festive order now spanning sweets, party supplies, fashion and precious metals. The figures are platform-reported activity, not a measure of India's whole Diwali retail market.

The Sweets League Table

On Instamart, kaju katli topped the mithai rankings, followed by motichoor laddoo and besan laddoo. Zepto's pattern differed: laddoo was its most frequently ordered mithai, while soan papdi, the Diwali gifting staple that travels in bulk, led in total quantity sold. Instamart's busiest shopping hour on November 8 was 11 a.m. to noon, with 11:18 a.m. its single busiest minute. Diet Coke, of all things, was the platform's most popular non-grocery item on Diwali eve, a detail Lapaas Voice's roundup of the platform data also highlighted.

"Gold coin orders on Instamart rose 23 times in the week leading up to Dhanteras and silver coin orders seven times; Mumbai recorded the biggest reported festive basket, at Rs 1.11 lakh of gold coins."

Party Orders and Hampers

The platforms' growth figures point the same way. Instamart reported a 162 percent year-on-year increase in party-planning orders and a 42 percent rise in snack and munchies orders. Zepto's festive hamper orders tripled compared with last Diwali, its diya orders reached 4.68 lakh over the festive period, and orders for flowers and garlands grew 2.5 times year on year, BusinessLine reported.

Gold, Delivered in Minutes

The sharpest change was at the top of the basket. Around Dhanteras, the traditional day for buying precious metal, Instamart's gold coin orders increased 23 times in the week leading up to the festival and silver coin orders rose seven times. One-gram coins were the most popular denomination. Floral designs accounted for nearly two-thirds of gold coins bought, while Lakshmi-Ganesh designs made up 73 percent of silver coin purchases. Mumbai recorded the biggest reported festive basket: Rs 1.11 lakh, largely gold coins in Lakshmi-Ganesh and lotus designs.

What It Adds Up To

None of this replaces the mithai shop or the jeweller; the platforms' own numbers describe their slice of the festival. But the slice keeps widening into categories, festive hampers, ethnic wear, and now Dhanteras gold, that quick commerce was not built for. For diaspora readers, the practical read is that the gift sent to family in India this Diwali was increasingly not a parcel at all, but an app order placed the same morning.
